title: Ethiopian Economics Entrance Exam 2017
description: Ethiopian Economics Entrance Exam 2017 - 85 multiple choice questions. Ethiopian national exam preparation material.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a determinant of aggregate demand?
options: Availability of credit
Cost of inputs
State of technology
Change in productivity
questions.explanation:
Determinants of Aggregate Demand (AD) are factors that affect the total spending in the economy (Consumption, Investment, Government Spending, and Net Exports).

 The Availability of credit affects consumption and investment spending, making it an AD determinant. Cost of inputs, State of technology, and Change in productivity are determinants of Aggregate Supply (AS).

questions.questionText: What is the effect of an exogenous increase in government spending?
options: Aggregate demand shifts to the right increasing both output and price level.
Aggregate demand shifts to the left decreasing both output and price level.
Aggregate demand shifts to the left decreasing output and increasing price level.
Aggregate demand shifts to the right increasing output but decreasing price level.
questions.explanation:
Government spending is a component of Aggregate Demand (AD). An exogenous increase (a change that comes from outside the model, like a policy decision) in government spending directly increases total spending in the economy.

 This causes the Aggregate Demand curve to shift to the right. In the standard Aggregate Demand-Aggregate Supply (AD-AS) model, a rightward shift in AD leads to an increase in both the equilibrium output (or GDP) and the price level.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about factors affecting aggregate supply?
options: Higher price of imported raw materials leads to firms to produce more.
Lower demand for commodities in the market initiates firms to produce more.
Subsidizing domestic industry in technology leads to decrease production.
Qualified high managerial ability leads to firms to produce more production.
questions.explanation:
Factors that increase aggregate supply include improvements in productivity, skilled management, and technological advancement.

 Qualified high managerial ability helps firms organize resources efficiently and increase production.

questions.questionText: Among the following statements, which one is correct about the short-run aggregate supply curve?
options: It shows the quantity demanded at different price levels, ceteris paribus.
It reveals that as price level rises, firms decrease the quantity supplied of goods.
It shows the quantity supplied of output at various price levels, ceteris paribus.
It reveals that as price level drops, firms increase the quantity supplied of goods.
questions.explanation:
The short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve shows the relationship between the overall price level and the quantity of goods and services that firms are willing to supply, holding all else constant (ceteris paribus).

 As price levels rise, firms are generally willing to supply more output in the short run.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about short-run equilibrium in the economy?
options: The occurrence of a shortage of goods leads to firms decrease output and consumption decrease consumption.
It is the intersection of aggregate demand and aggregate supply.
The occurrence of a surplus of goods leads to firms decrease output and consumption increase consumption.
It is the intersection of long-run and short-run aggregate supply curves.
questions.explanation: Short-run equilibrium in an economy occurs where the aggregate demand (AD) curve intersects the short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve. At this point, the quantity of goods and services demanded equals the quantity supplied in the short run.

questions.questionText: Suppose the price level changed from the equilibrium of aggregate demand and short run aggregate supply in an economy. Which of the following is true about the result?
options: At a lower price level, there will be surplus, and the price level decreases.
At a higher price level there will be shortage, and the price level increases.
At a lower price level, there will be shortage and the price level rises.
At a higher price level there will be surplus, and the price level increases.
questions.explanation:
If the price level deviates from the short-run equilibrium, market forces push it back. 

At a lower price level than equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, creating a shortage, which drives the price level up.

 Conversely, at a higher price level than equilibrium, quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, creating a surplus, which pushes the price level down.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly describe market failure?
options: The individual incentives for rational behavior lead to rational outcomes for the group.
The price mechanisms accounts for all the costs and benefits to provide and consume a good.
The steady state equilibrium in which quantity supplied is equal to quantity demanded.
The inefficient distribution of goods and services in the free market.
questions.explanation:
Market failure occurs when the free market fails to allocate resources efficiently, leading to an inefficient distribution of goods and services.

 This can happen due to externalities, public goods, monopolies, or information asymmetries

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a solution for the market failure caused by a firm that pollutes a river?
options: Taxing the polluting firm
Subsidizing the polluting firm
Encouraging the polluting firm
Renting the polluted river
questions.explanation:
When a firm pollutes a river, it creates a negative externality, which is a form of market failure.

 A common solution is to impose a tax on the polluting firm, which internalizes the external cost and incentivizes the firm to reduce pollution.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following explains the free rider problem in an economy?
options: free ridership is a problem that arises due to the excludable nature of public goods.
Individuals get the benefits of public goods without contributing anything to the cost.
All individuals have the incentive to pay for the public good.
The free rider problem enables the markets operate efficiently for public goods.
questions.explanation:
The free rider problem occurs when individuals can enjoy the benefits of a public good without paying for it.

 Since public goods are non-excludable, people may choose not to contribute, relying on others to cover the cost, which leads to under-provision of the good.

questions.questionText: Among the following alternatives, which one represents a positive externality?
options: Playing loud music in the neighborhood
Smoking in public places
Vaccination program in the neighborhood
Overgrazing cows in the common pasture lands
questions.explanation:
A positive externality occurs when an activity provides benefits to third parties who are not directly involved.

 Vaccination programs help protect not only the vaccinated individuals but also reduce the spread of disease to others in the community, creating a positive spillover effect.

questions.questionText: Asymmetric information is a situation when:
options: buyers and sellers have different type of information.
buyers and sellers have the same type of information.
buyers and sellers want to be free riders.
buyers and sellers lack agreement on the price.
questions.explanation:
Asymmetric information occurs when one party in a transaction has more or better information than the other.

 This imbalance can lead to market inefficiencies, such as adverse selection or moral hazard.

questions.questionText: When an individual builds on their skills by acquiring more education/training, the individual is trying to
options: free ride the employer.
screen the employer.
create externality for the employer.
signal to the employer.
questions.explanation:
When a person gains more education or training, they are often signaling their productivity and skills to potential employers.

 This helps employers identify qualified candidates, which is known as 'signaling' in labor economics.

questions.questionText: Why is it necessary the need for consumer protection?
options: Consumers often do not exercise their rights.
Sellers compete with each other aggressively.
Consumers' interest and business survival are unrelated.
Consumers have the same information as sellers.
questions.explanation:
Consumer protection is needed because consumers usually have less information than sellers and may not exercise their rights effectively.

 This ensures fair trade, safety, and prevents exploitation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is among the general objectives of macroeconomic policy?
options: Cost minimization
Income inequality
Healthy balance of payment
Profit maximization
questions.explanation:
A key objective of macroeconomic policy is to maintain a healthy balance of payments, ensuring that a country's international trade and financial transactions are sustainable.

 This helps stabilize the economy and supports growth.

questions.questionText: Among the following alternatives, which one is a monetary policy tool?
options: Taxation
Discount rate
Transfer payments
Grants in aid
questions.explanation:
Monetary policy tools are instruments used by the central bank to regulate money supply and credit in the economy.

 The discount rate is a key monetary policy tool as it influences the cost of borrowing for commercial banks, which in turn affects lending and economic activity.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT a financial sector reform component of the macroeconomic reforms of the Home Grown Economic Reforms?
options: Reduce the supply of credit to the private sector
Promote market based interest rate
Strengthen the capacity of the National Bank of Ethiopia
Establish and expand capital markets
questions.explanation:
Financial sector reforms under the Home Grown Economic Reforms aim to strengthen financial institutions, promote efficient allocation of credit, establish market-based interest rates, and develop capital markets.

 Reducing the supply of credit to the private sector contradicts these objectives and is therefore NOT a reform component.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an advantage of fiscal decentralization?
options: Local externalities
Inefficient tax system
Ineffectiveness of redistributing program
Fostering intergovernmental competition
questions.explanation:
Fiscal decentralization allows local governments to manage resources and policies suited to their local needs.

 One advantage is that it fosters intergovernmental competition, encouraging efficiency and innovation among local authorities.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true regarding the link between population growth and the environment?
options: Rapid population growth reduces disguised unemployment and increases per capita product/output.
Rapid population growth accompanied by heavy rural-urban migration could lead to urban pollution.
Rapid population growth leads to capital formation and accelerated rural development due to high propensity to save and invest.
Rapid population growth enables improvement in land to man ratio due to the elastic supply of land.
questions.explanation: Rapid population growth, especially when coupled with rural-urban migration, can strain urban infrastructure and resources, resulting in environmental issues such as air and water pollution, traffic congestion, and inadequate waste management.

questions.questionText: Rural development is a strategy focused on
options: capital intensive resources
technology intensive resources
increasing rural-urban migration
the utilization of natural resources
questions.explanation: Rural development strategies aim to improve the livelihoods of rural populations by efficiently utilizing natural resources, enhancing agricultural productivity, and promoting sustainable development in rural areas.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following best describe climate change?
options: persistent variation in the mean state of climate
short lived change in the weather from day to day
decline in forest coverage through deforestation
Release of greenhouse gases in to the atmosphere
questions.explanation: Climate change refers to long-term and persistent changes in the average state of the climate, including temperature, precipitation, and other atmospheric conditions, rather than short-term weather variations or specific causes like deforestation or greenhouse gas release alone.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about income policy?
options: It stabilizes wages and prices.
It facilitates money supply.
It stabilizes the interest rate.
It encourages reduction of taxes.
questions.explanation:
Income policy is a government measure aimed at controlling inflation by directly regulating wages and prices to prevent them from rising too rapidly.

 It does not directly affect money supply, interest rates, or tax rates.

questions.questionText: Consider the market for teff, what will be the impact of a government imposition of a price floor?
options: The price floor is below the equilibrium price of teff resulting in shortage of teff.
The price floor is above the equilibrium price of teff resulting in shortage of teff.
The price floor is below the equilibrium price of teff resulting in surplus of teff.
The price floor is above the equilibrium price of teff resulting in surplus of teff.
questions.explanation:
A price floor is a legally set minimum price above the equilibrium price. 

If the government sets a price floor above the equilibrium, the price is higher than what buyers are willing to pay at equilibrium, leading to excess supply or a surplus of teff.

 If the price floor is below equilibrium, it has no effect.

questions.questionText: In a free market for labor, the wage rate is determined such that
options: the demand of labor is greater than the supply of labor.
perfect, costless information and labour mobility.
the government sets the minimum wage.
the supply of labor is greater than the demand for labor.
questions.explanation:
In a free labor market, wages are determined by the intersection of labor demand and labor supply.

 This assumes that workers and employers have perfect information and can move freely, allowing the market to reach equilibrium without government interference.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the disadvantage of the floating exchange rate regime?
options: Correction of balance of payments deficits
Protection from external shocks
Governments are free to pursue other policies
Instability and uncertainty facing firms and consumers
questions.explanation: While a floating exchange rate allows automatic adjustment of balance of payments and policy freedom, it can create instability and uncertainty for businesses and consumers due to fluctuating currency values.

questions.questionText: What is the correct name for a decrease in the exchange rate due to market forces?
options: Depreciation
Devaluation
Appreciation
Revaluation
questions.explanation:
A decrease in the exchange rate caused by market forces (supply and demand for currency) is called depreciation.

 Devaluation, on the other hand, is a deliberate reduction by the government.

questions.questionText: Among the following statements, which one is correct about taxation?
options: It is payment made to government to obtain direct benefit in return.
It is the compulsory, unrequited payments to general government.
It is payments that individuals make to government if they want.
It is the only source of revenue for the government for personal use.
questions.explanation:
Taxation is defined as a compulsory payment made by individuals or organizations to the government without a direct benefit in return.

 It is not voluntary and not solely for personal government use.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the main objective of taxation?
options: Stabilizing the economy
Minimizing income equalities
Encouraging import
Reducing regional balance
questions.explanation: The main objective of taxation is to stabilize the economy by generating revenue for government spending, influencing economic activity, and controlling inflation or deflation.

questions.questionText: In United Kingdom (UK), what is the main objective of a "sin tax" on products like tobacco?
options: Encouraging administrative efficiency
Encouraging consumption
Reducing consumption
Stabilizing the economy
questions.explanation: A 'sin tax' is imposed on products that are harmful to health, like tobacco and alcohol, with the primary goal of reducing their consumption by making them more expensive.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following correctly states about tax incidence?
options: It relates to the way the burden of tax is distributed among economic units.
It points out who is illegally responsible for paying the tax from the income.
It is imposing high taxes on high-income earners without any consideration.
It is the way of discouraging low-income earners from paying taxes.
questions.explanation: Tax incidence refers to how the burden of a tax is shared between buyers and sellers or among different groups in the economy, regardless of who formally pays the tax.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the characteristic feature of a good tax system?
options: It creates income inequalities.
It is complex and financially inelastic.
It enables optimum allocation of resources.
It is narrow based-tax and is levied only on income.
questions.explanation: A good tax system should promote efficiency, equity, and simplicity. One key feature is that it helps in the optimum allocation of resources by not distorting economic decisions unnecessarily.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the focus area of macroeconomics?
options: Profit maximization of a corporation
The growth of a firm in the economy
Cost minimization of a specific company
Inflation caused by different factors
questions.explanation:
Macroeconomics studies the overall economy and its large-scale phenomena, such as inflation, unemployment, and national output.

 Unlike microeconomics, it does not focus on individual firms or profit maximization.

questions.questionText: In which of the following macroeconomics is different from microeconomics?
options: Studying about the performance of individual firm
Studying about the behavior of the aggregate economy
Analyzing about the actions of individual company
Focusing on the specific price of products
questions.explanation: Macroeconomics focuses on the behavior and performance of the entire economy, including aggregates like GDP, inflation, and unemployment, whereas microeconomics studies individual firms, households, and prices of specific goods

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a key challenge of macroeconomics?
options: Income and consumption pattern of a given household
The total amount of laborers hired by a given industry
The amount of profit earned by a given firm
The number of unemployed people in a given country
questions.explanation: Macroeconomics deals with aggregate variables in the economy. Challenges include issues like unemployment, inflation, and overall economic growth, rather than individual household income or firm profit.

questions.questionText: Balance of trade of a country is the difference between
options: gross domestic product and gross national product.
private and public businesses and transfers.
trade surplus and trade deficit.
export and import earning from goods and services.
questions.explanation:
The balance of trade measures the difference between the value of a country's exports and imports of goods and services.

 A positive balance indicates a trade surplus, while a negative balance indicates a trade deficit.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following school of macroeconomic thought was predominant until the occurrence of the Great Depression?
options: Monetarist
Keynesian
Classical
New Keynesian
questions.explanation:
Before the Great Depression of the 1930s, the Classical school of economics dominated.

 It emphasized that markets are self-correcting, flexible prices and wages ensure full employment, and government intervention is unnecessary.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the view of Classical theory?
options: Fiscal policy is useful to influence output.
Recession is a temporary phenomenon.
Monetary policy can influence output.
There is a need of cutting government spending.
questions.explanation:
Classical theory believes that markets are self-correcting, and any recession is temporary.

 Flexible prices and wages restore full employment without government intervention.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following macroeconomic school stressed the existence of nominal rigidities arising from nominal wage contracts?
options: The new Classical
Keynesian
The classical
The monetarist
questions.explanation: The Keynesian school emphasizes that wages and prices are sticky in the short run due to contracts and other frictions, which can prevent markets from clearing and cause unemployment.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about the differences between monetarist and Keynesian school of thought?
options: Keynesians argued that aggregate demand is always automatically high.
Monetarists argued that fiscal policy addresses macroeconomic problems.
Keynesians argued that monetary policy stimulates aggregate demand.
Monetarist argued that monetary policy addresses macroeconomic problems.
questions.explanation: Monetarists, led by Milton Friedman, emphasize that controlling the money supply is the primary tool to manage the economy, whereas Keynesians focus more on fiscal policy and government intervention to influence aggregate demand.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following best describes about aggregate demand in a given country?
options: It is the total expenditure of households and government on goods and services in a given period.
It is the total amount that households and firms willingly spend on the country's goods and services in a given period.
It is total demand by **households, firms and government** on the goods and services in a given period.
It is total spending by firms and government on the economy's goods and services in a given period.
questions.explanation:
Aggregate demand represents the total demand for all goods and services in an economy, coming from households, firms, and government within a specific period.

 This includes consumption, investment, and government spending.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about factors affecting household consumption expenditure?
options: Expectation of a lower future income increases consumption.
Decreases in wealth lead to increase in consumption.
Increases in interest rate decreases consumption.
Increases in income taxes decreases consumption.
questions.explanation:
Household consumption is influenced by factors like income, taxes, interest rates, and wealth. 

Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive and saving more attractive, which reduces consumption. Similarly, higher income taxes reduce disposable income and decrease consumption.

questions.questionText: What type of policy that aims at changing government spending?
options: Exchange rate policy
Monetary policy
Fiscal policy
Property rights policy
questions.explanation:
Fiscal policy refers to the use of government spending and taxation to influence the overall economy.

 When the government changes its spending levels, it directly affects aggregate demand, economic growth, and employment levels.

questions.questionText: In a situation when an economy is facing the problem of deficient demand, what will happen to the economy?
options: Depression marked by a decline in unemployment
Depression marked by underproduction
Depression marked by fall in incomes
Enjoyment marked by a fall in prices
questions.explanation:
When an economy suffers from deficient demand, total demand in the economy is insufficient to purchase all the goods and services produced.

 This leads to lower production, falling incomes, and often higher unemployment, resulting in an economic depression.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is important role of fiscal policy in an economy?
options: Increasing people's income by increasing taxes
Increasing government expenditure to solve recession
Solving trade deficit by increasing imports
Increasing government expenditure to control inflation
questions.explanation:
Fiscal policy involves government spending and taxation to influence the economy.

 During a recession, aggregate demand is low. Increasing government expenditure stimulates demand, encourages production, and helps reduce unemployment. Options A and C would contract demand, and D is generally used to fight inflation rather than recession.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true regarding the impact of monetary policy on aggregate demand?
options: lowering interest rate decreases aggregate demand.
Increasing the discount rate increases aggregate demand.
An increase in money supply decreases aggregate demand.
An increase in money supply increases aggregate demand.
questions.explanation:
Monetary policy influences aggregate demand through changes in money supply and interest rates.

 An increase in the money supply lowers interest rates, making borrowing cheaper, which encourages spending and investment, thereby increasing aggregate demand.

 Options A, B, and C describe effects that are opposite to the actual relationship.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the main issue of macroeconomic policy?
options: Maximizing firm's profit
Controlling inflation
Encouraging firm's competition
Restructuring the market
questions.explanation:
Macroeconomic policy focuses on overall economic stability, including controlling inflation, unemployment, and promoting sustainable growth.

 Unlike microeconomic goals that focus on individual firms, macroeconomic policy targets aggregate outcomes like price stability, which is why controlling inflation is the correct choice.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the objective of the national long-term plan after the reform of 2021-2030?
options: Expanding access to education and health services and achieving MDGs
Launching strategy of Agricultural Development Led Industrialization
Maintaining macroeconomic stability, ensuring rapid sustainable economic growth and creating decent job
Speed up and catalyze transformation of the domestic private sector and render them a capable development force
questions.explanation:
The national long-term plan after the 2021-2030 reform focuses on overall economic stability, sustainable growth, and job creation.

 While education, health, and private sector development are important, the core objective centers on macroeconomic stability and economic growth that generates decent employment.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following was a crucial component of the second five year plan during the monarchy regime?
options: Enhancement of technical and vocational education
Overvalued currency and implemented pricing policies
Transition from an agricultural economy to an agro-industry
Strengthened a political system that guaranteed administrative justice
questions.explanation:
The second five-year plan of the imperial period in Ethiopia focused on structural transformation of the economy.

 A key component was shifting from a primarily agricultural economy toward agro-industry to boost industrialization and reduce dependence on raw agriculture.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following was the challenges Ethiopia encountered with during its implementation of the Growth and Transformation Plans I and II?
options: Sluggish structural transformation and weak sectorial linkages
Actual growth performance was higher than the annual target
The contribution of the service sector to the overall GDP was the highest.
The contribution of each sector to the overall economy was uniformly low.
questions.explanation:
During the implementation of Ethiopia's Growth and Transformation Plans (GTP I and II), one of the main challenges was that structural transformation was slow, and sectoral linkages, especially between agriculture and industry, were weak.

 This limited the full potential of economic growth and industrialization.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about the key strategic pillars of the ten-year development plan after reform?
options: Building regional monopoly power and economy
Quality economic growth and shared prosperity
Public sector-led economic growth
Gender and social exclusion
questions.explanation:
The ten-year national development plan after the reform emphasizes sustainable and quality economic growth alongside ensuring shared prosperity.

 These strategic pillars aim to boost inclusive growth, reduce poverty, and enhance equitable development across the country.

questions.questionText: Among the followings, which one is the objective of the Home Grown Economic Reform?
options: Encouraging debt vulnerabilities.
Creating inadequate job opportunities.
Transition from private to public sector-led growth.
Maintaining macroeconomic stability.
questions.explanation:
The Home Grown Economic Reform in Ethiopia aims to ensure macroeconomic stability by promoting sustainable growth, reducing fiscal imbalances, and creating a conducive environment for private sector-led development.

 It is designed to strengthen economic resilience rather than encourage debt or create inadequate job opportunities.

questions.questionText: One of the following correctly describes weather. Which one is it?
options: It is unpredictable atmospheric conditions.
It is short-term atmospheric conditions.
It is rainy season occurs for long period of time.
It is long-term atmospheric conditions.
questions.explanation:
Weather refers to the short-term state of the atmosphere in a particular place at a particular time, including conditions like temperature, humidity, precipitation, and wind.

 Unlike climate, which describes long-term patterns, weather is temporary and changes daily or hourly.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true regarding the link between global warming and climate change?
options: Greenhouse gases raise atmospheric temperatures and produce other changes in the climate system.
Global warming is unrelated to human activities emitting greenhouse gases.
There is no link between economic activity and energy emission through the greenhouse effect.
Burning of fossil fuels and reductions of forests that sink carbon dioxide decreases greenhouse gases.
questions.explanation:
Global warming refers to the increase in Earth's average temperature due to human-induced greenhouse gas emissions.

 This rise in temperature triggers broader changes in the climate system, including shifts in precipitation patterns, sea level rise, and more extreme weather events.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following shows the impact of environmental degradation and climate change on economic growth?
options: Improvement of food security due to length of growing seasons in arid areas
Long-term changes influencing agriculture, water, health and other sectors
Use of biologically renewable resources and renewable physical stock
Improvement in the economic well-being of the rural people
questions.explanation: Environmental degradation and climate change negatively affect economic growth by disrupting agriculture, water availability, health, and other vital sectors, leading to reduced productivity, higher costs, and slower economic development.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of mitigation strategy to tackle climate change?
options: Subsidizing the use of fossil fuels
Reducing the role of indigenous communities
Destabilizing greenhouse gases
Reducing the release of carbon dioxide (CO2)
questions.explanation:
Mitigation strategies aim to reduce or prevent the emission of greenhouse gases. 

Reducing CO2 emissions directly addresses the root cause of climate change by lowering the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is responsible for an active economic activity and emission resulting in global warming?
options: Green growth strategies
Greenhouse gases
Mitigation policies
Carbon taxes
questions.explanation:
Greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide and methane, are emitted through various human economic activities like industry, transport, and energy production.

 These gases trap heat in the atmosphere, leading to global warming.

questions.questionText: Among the following statements, which one is correct about mitigation strategy to address climate change?
options: It adjusts to the potential impacts of climate change.
It emits the same amount of pollution across all countries.
It involves long-term limits on the amount of greenhouse emissions.
It intensives use of non-renewable resources of energy.
questions.explanation: Mitigation strategies aim to reduce or limit the emission of greenhouse gases over the long term to prevent or slow down climate change, rather than adapting to its effects.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following describes green economy?
options: It is characterized by loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services.
It emits higher percentage of greenhouse gas than other economies.
It uses high carbon, is resource inefficient and socially exclusive.
It reduces environmental risk and ecological scarcity to improve well-being.
questions.explanation: A green economy focuses on sustainable development by reducing environmental risks, conserving resources, and promoting social inclusivity to enhance overall well-being.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT a source of renewable energy?
options: Solar energy
Fossil fuel energy
Wind energy
Thermal energy
questions.explanation:
Fossil fuels such as coal, oil, and natural gas are non-renewable energy sources because they take millions of years to form and are depleted when used.

 Renewable energy sources include solar, wind, and thermal energy from natural, replenishable processes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about green growth?
options: It relies on eroding the natural capital.
It is a carbon intensive growth strategy.
It employs renewable energy and low carbon.
It exacerbates environmental related risks.
questions.explanation: Green growth focuses on promoting economic growth and development while ensuring that natural resources are used sustainably, employing renewable energy sources and low-carbon strategies to reduce environmental impact.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT a key cause of Ethiopia's vulnerability to climate change as indicated in the policy documents of the country?
options: High population growth
Dependence on rain-fed agriculture
Carbon emission from rapid industrialization
Poor water resource development
questions.explanation:
Ethiopia's climate vulnerability is primarily linked to high population growth, dependence on rain-fed agriculture, and poor water resource development.

 Rapid industrial carbon emissions are not considered a major cause of vulnerability in the country's policy documents, as Ethiopia's industrial base is relatively small compared to developed nations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following tax approach has the advantage of linking tax equity with the expenditure side of the public budget?
options: The benefits approach
The ability to pay approach
The approach based on vertical equity
The approach based on horizontal equity
questions.explanation:
The benefits approach to taxation links the amount of tax paid by individuals to the benefits they receive from public services. 

This approach aligns tax equity with public expenditure, ensuring that those who benefit more from government services contribute proportionally to their cost.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the nature of tax system in Ethiopia?
options: The regional governments are solely responsible for tax collection.
The federal government is solely responsible for tax collection.
The federal and regional governments share tax revenue and manage their budgets.
The federal government levies taxes on behalf of the regional governments.
questions.explanation:
Ethiopia operates a federal system where both the federal and regional governments have the authority to levy taxes and manage their own budgets.

 This allows for fiscal decentralization and shared responsibility in revenue generation.

questions.questionText: In Ethiopia, which of the following is correct regarding the turnover tax?
options: tax levied on persons unregistered for value added tax.
tax imposed on goods that are hazardous to harmful products.
tax levied on the values added at every stage.
tax imposed on income from employment.
questions.explanation:
Turnover tax in Ethiopia is applied to businesses that are not registered for VAT.

 It is levied on the total sales or turnover of such businesses, providing a simple tax mechanism for small and medium enterprises that are below the VAT registration threshold.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the correct definition of tax evasion?
options: Falsifying information on tax return to reduce one's tax liability
Taking full advantage of tax provisions to reduce one's tax obligations
Paying the same share of tax regardless of income
The degree of complexity in the tax administration system
questions.explanation:
Tax evasion refers to the illegal practice of deliberately falsifying or concealing information on tax returns to reduce tax liability.

 This is distinct from tax avoidance, which is legally using provisions in the tax law to minimize taxes.

questions.questionText: What is the reason for poverty to be considered as a multidimensional concept?
options: It is based on a single dimension.
It is adequately measured with income.
It only measures quantitative related difference.
It depends on several related deprivations.
questions.explanation:
Poverty is considered multidimensional because it is not only about low income but also about lack of access to education, health care, clean water, housing, and other essential resources. 

Measuring poverty requires assessing multiple dimensions of deprivation.

questions.questionText: In the steps listed for measuring poverty, what does the first step says that 'defining an indicator of welfare' describe?
options: Specifying a minimal socially acceptable level of income or consumption
Implementing a representative survey in which consumption is measured
Taking the first step of measurement to know which people are rich
Choosing and calculating a specific poverty measurement
questions.explanation:
The first step in measuring poverty, 'defining an indicator of welfare,' involves deciding what constitutes well-being in the society.

 Typically, this is done by specifying a minimal level of income or consumption considered socially acceptable, which becomes the benchmark for identifying who is poor.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is in comparison to other people's standing in the economy?
options: Poverty headcount index
Absolute poverty
Relative poverty
Multidimensional poverty
questions.explanation:
Relative poverty measures an individual's or household's economic status in comparison to the wider society. 

Unlike absolute poverty, which is based on a fixed minimum standard, relative poverty considers inequality and how a person's resources compare to others in the economy.

questions.questionText: Among the following statements, which one is correct regarding absolute poverty?
options: The comparison of an individual to other people's standing in the economy
The situation of someone being unable to meet the subsistence basic needs
The explanation of matter of failure of distributive justice
The description of an individual able to command sufficient resources
questions.explanation:
Absolute poverty refers to a condition where an individual or household cannot afford the basic necessities required for survival, such as food, shelter, and clothing.

 It is measured against a fixed threshold and does not depend on the economic status of others.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following deals with households and the total incomes they receive regardless of the way in which they received that income?
options: Social inequality of community
Size distribution of income
Functional distribution of income
Factor share distribution of income
questions.explanation:
The size distribution of income focuses on how total income is distributed among households, without considering the source of that income.

 It analyzes income inequality by comparing the incomes of different households within an economy.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about the status of women in relation to men in development?
options: Women have stable sources of income.
Women's earning potential is higher.
Intra-household resource allocation favors women.
Women are much less likely to be in formal jobs.
questions.explanation: In many developing countries, women face barriers to formal employment, limited access to education, and unequal opportunities compared to men, which reduces their participation in the formal labor market.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following country made significant progress in reducing poverty over the past half century?
options: China
Eritrea
India
Bangladesh
questions.explanation: China has experienced rapid economic growth and development over the past 50 years, lifting hundreds of millions of people out of poverty, making it one of the most notable examples of poverty reduction globally.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about the poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa?
options: The majority of people on less than $1.90 a day live in the region.
The region experienced significant reduction in poverty in the last 20 years.
The region has managed to escape the problem of poverty.
The region has lifted millions of citizens out of poverty in the last decade.
questions.explanation:
Sub-Saharan Africa remains the region with the highest concentration of extreme poverty globally.

 A large portion of the world's population living under $1.90 per day resides in this region, despite some progress in poverty reduction.

questions.questionText: What is the main advantage of cottage industries in reducing poverty?
options: It employs capital intensive techniques.
It has insignificant contribution to economies.
It offers self-development exclusively for women.
It employs labor intensive techniques.
questions.explanation:
Cottage industries are small-scale, labor-intensive enterprises that provide employment opportunities for many people, including those with limited skills or capital.

 This makes them effective in reducing poverty by creating jobs and income at the local level.

questions.questionText: what was the goal of sustainable development and poverty reduction program (SDPRP) assigned by Ethiopian Peoples' Revolutionary democratic Front?
options: building all-inclusive implementation capacity
Capacity building in the public and private sector
massive push to accelerate economic growth
Unleashing the potentials of Ethiopia's women
questions.explanation: The SDPRP aimed primarily to accelerate economic growth and reduce poverty in Ethiopia by implementing targeted development programs and policies that improved productivity and livelihoods across sectors.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following was the objective of the third five year plan during the imperial period (1968-1973)?
options: Establishment of cadre of skilled and semi-skilled personnel to work in processing industries.
Development of a strong infrastructure (transportation, construction, communication).
Expansion of educational opportunities and improvement in peasant agriculture.
Acceleration of agricultural development by promoting commercial agricultural venture.
questions.explanation: The Third Five Year Plan (1968-1973) in Ethiopia focused on improving agricultural productivity and expanding educational opportunities to support rural development and address food shortages, reflecting the government's emphasis on peasant agriculture.

questions.questionText: The unemployment rate for an economy is 4%. The labor force is estimated to be 55 million.What is the number of unemployed people in millions?
options: 2.2 million
220 million
20 million
22 million
questions.explanation: The number of unemployed people can be calculated using the formula: Unemployed = Unemployment rate × Labor force. Here, 4% of 55 million = 0.04 × 55,000,000 = 2,200,000, which is 2.2 million.

questions.questionText: What is an income tax of an employee works in the one of Ethiopian government development organization with salary of Birr 36,000?
options: Birr 12,600
Birr 11,100
Birr 26,400
Birr 24,900
questions.explanation: Assuming Ethiopia's progressive income tax rates, the tax for an annual salary of Birr 36,000 is calculated based on the applicable brackets, resulting in a total tax liability of Birr 11,100.

questions.questionText: Suppose the area between the line of complete equality (45 degree) and the Lorenz curve is 60 units. Additionally the whole area below the line of equality (45 degree) is 150 units. What is the Gini-coefficient?
questions.explanation:
The Gini coefficient is calculated as the ratio of the area between the line of equality and the Lorenz curve to the total area under the line of equality.

 Here, Gini = 60 / 150 = 0.4.

questions.questionText: Suppose the adult population in a given country is estimated at 105 million. The total number of employed and unemployed individuals is estimated at 55 million and 8 million respectively. What is the labor force participation rate?
questions.explanation:
Labor force participation rate (LFPR) is calculated as: LFPR = (Labor Force / Adult Population) × 100.

 Labor Force = Employed + Unemployed = 55 + 8 = 63 million. LFPR = (63 / 105) × 100 ≈ 60%.

questions.questionText: In November 2010, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for a country was 100. In November 2011, the Consumer Price Index CPI for the same country was 130. What was the inflation rate for 2011?
questions.explanation:
The inflation rate is calculated using the formula: Inflation Rate = ((CPI_current - CPI_previous) / CPI_previous) × 100.

 Here, ((130 - 100) / 100) × 100 = 

(30 / 100) × 100 = 30%

questions.questionText: Which of the following increase consumption?
options: An increase in future price
decrease in future income
An increase in business taxes
decrease in wealth
questions.explanation:
An expectation of higher future prices can lead households to increase current consumption to avoid paying more later.

 Conversely, decreases in future income, higher taxes, or loss of wealth generally reduce consumption.

questions.questionText: What is the economic terminology for the situation where non-smokers suffer by the air contamination induced by smokers?
options: Non-excludable
Free rider
Asymmetric information
Externality
questions.explanation:
An externality occurs when the actions of one individual or firm affect the well-being of others without compensation. 

In this case, smokers create a negative externality by polluting the air, harming non-smokers.

questions.questionText: How should taxes be distributed in case of the ability-to-pay approach to taxes?
options: As per the capacity of tax payers to pay
In line with the benefits derived from public services
Ease of tax administration
Expenditure side of the budget
questions.explanation:
The ability-to-pay principle of taxation states that taxes should be levied according to an individual's or entity's capacity to bear the tax burden.

 Wealthier individuals pay more, while those with lower income pay less, ensuring equity in the tax system.

questions.questionText: Which of the following refer to the capability approach of studying poverty?
options: Income and wealth
Headcount index
Ability to function
Comparison to others
questions.explanation:
The capability approach, developed by Amartya Sen, focuses on what individuals are able to do and be — their capabilities — rather than just income or resources.

 Poverty is assessed based on deprivation in these essential capabilities.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the role of the traditional institution of Iqub in reducing poverty in Ethiopia?
options: Borrowed ideas from the western world
Pooling resources for a common good
Being top down societal organization
Having limited role in development
questions.explanation:
Iqub is a traditional Ethiopian rotating savings and credit association where members pool resources and provide loans to each other.

 This institution helps households access credit, smooth consumption, and reduce poverty at the community level.
